core.title: Token and foundation files hold values, not behaviour
core.given: A code file in the value layers of the design system (the `tokens` or `foundations` layer beneath the design root identified by the profile)
core.when: The file exists in the repository, existing or newly written, and the design-system check scans it
core.then: The file contains only values (palette, spacing, radii, motion, scales): it imports no renderer, renders no markup, and branches with no control flow.
prefer: Keep tokens/foundations value-only; move markup to the layers above them (primitives/components) and behaviour to the layer that owns it
During GREEN: leave the value in the token or foundation file
During GREEN: move only the markup or logic the current behaviour requires to the nearest existing owning layer
During GREEN: reuse an existing primitive or component before creating a new one
avoid: Moving behaviour into a different layer merely to silence the rule
Creating a generalized component unrelated to the current acceptance
unless: Test files and vendored/build trees are never scanned
Token files in the stack's declarative token form (the profile's declarative token form) are values by construction and are not scanned
A repository with no design root is not judged (self-scoping)
core.why: Tokens are what every other layer depends on; once they render or decide, the bottom of the hierarchy has behaviour and every primitive inherits it.
evidence: The current behavioural or rendering acceptance passes
Token and foundation code files remain value-only: the design-system check reports no renderer imports, rendered markup or control flow in them
verification: The check scans token/foundation code files for renderer imports (the profile's renderer import set), rendered markup, and control-flow branching (the profile's value-file control-flow constructs); it applies to every in-scope file, existing or newly written
A repository with no design root is not judged (self-scoping): there is no system to connect to yet

A pure token is a declaration whose value is data — a string, number, or object of them, including references to other tokens as data (written in the stack's token-reference syntax); such declarations pass

The check does not cover test files (the union of the profile's unit-test, acceptance-test and e2e-test name patterns), vendored/build trees (never scanned; the checker owns the exact classification of vendored/build trees), or token files in the stack's declarative token form (the profile's declarative token form)

values: code (not a test file of any kind, not a declarative-token-form file)

fires: A code file in the token layer imports a renderer (one of the profile's renderer imports)
A foundations code file returns or renders markup
A token code file computes a value with control flow
An existing, unchanged token file already contains one of the above when the check runs
doesNotFire: The repository has no design root
A token file in the stack's declarative token form under the tokens layer
A test file of any kind (unit, acceptance or e2e), or a file in a vendored/build tree (excluded; the checker owns the exact classification)
Files in the primitives, components or templates layers
A token file declaring only strings, numbers, objects of them, or references to other tokens as data (in the stack's token-reference syntax)

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the design system lives: the directory names that mark the design root, and that the first directory beneath it names the design-system layer; only the value layers (tokens, foundations) are in this rule's scope, and a repository with no design root is out of scope (self-scoping).
profileRequirements.bunValue: Design root: a directory named `design`, `design_system`, or `design-system`; the first directory beneath it names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`. In-scope globs: `**/design/tokens/**`, `**/design/foundations/**`, `**/design_system/tokens/**`, `**/design_system/foundations/**`, `**/design-system/tokens/**`, `**/design-system/foundations/**`.

proposedKeys.meaning: Directory names that mark the design-system root; the first directory beneath it names the design-system layer (value layers: tokens/foundations; above them: primitives, components, templates). A repository with no design root is out of scope for design-system rules (self-scoping).
proposedKeys.bunValue: `design`, `design_system`, `design-system`; first directory beneath names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates` (in-scope globs: `**/design/tokens/**`, `**/design/foundations/**`, `**/design_system/tokens/**`, `**/design_system/foundations/**`, `**/design-system/tokens/**`, `**/design-system/foundations/**`)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The roles group only knows the ten architectural roles and their paths; there is no key for the design system's root directory or its layer segmentation, which design-system rules (tokens-pure, layer ordering) need to locate the value layers and to express self-scoping.

proposedKeys.meaning: Import specifiers that count as importing a renderer (a markup/rendering library) into a design-system value layer; presence in a token/foundation code file is the 'renderer import' finding.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.forbidden_runtime_imports is the stack-wide set of runtime/framework/transport imports forbidden to inner architectural roles; the renderer set for design value layers is a distinct predicate and the two need not coincide, so it must not be redefined to carry this list.

proposedKeys.meaning: The control-flow constructs prohibited in a design-system value (token/foundation) code file; presence of any of them is the 'control flow' finding.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.control_keywords is documented as the keywords counted toward nesting depth; the set of constructs prohibited in value files is a separate purity predicate that may have a different keyword set, so sharing the existing key would change its meaning.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's declarative token-authoring file form: token files of this form are values by construction and are never scanned by value-only checks.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No suffix.<file_kind> parametric kind describes a declarative token-authoring form (the closed kinds are source/test/markup/plan/config), and no idiom key describes it; the core's neutral exclusion needs this form as instantiation data rather than realization prose.

proposedKeys.meaning: The syntax by which a token declaration references another token as data; such references still count as values in the pure-token definition.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No idiom or suffix key describes how one token references another as data; the pure-token definition needs this syntax as instantiation data, and leaving it realization-only would leave the allowed-reference rule unbound to the profile.

neutralityNotes: Design-system layer names (tokens, foundations, primitives, components, templates) are treated as stack-neutral design-system vocabulary — the Vite twin shares them — so only directory shapes, file forms/patterns and import specifiers come from the profile or bunOnly. Test-file exclusions use the union of the three test-kind suffix keys (suffix.unit_test, suffix.acceptance_test, suffix.e2e_test), each keeping its own per-kind meaning; Bun merely applies the same pattern set (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) to all three kinds, so the same values instantiate each key without redefining any of them as an all-tests key. Five keys are proposed: layout.design_root (design-system root and layer segmentation), idiom.renderer_imports and idiom.value_control_flow (dedicated predicates instead of repurposing idiom.forbidden_runtime_imports / idiom.control_keywords, whose documented meanings differ), idiom.declarative_token_form (the `.css` declarative token form) and idiom.token_reference (the `var(--…)` reference syntax), binding the neutral exclusion and allowed-reference definition to profile data. No roots.excluded requirement is made: bun.json supplies only checker-owned classification of vendored/build exclusions, which stays in core:verification as deference. The remaining realization-only detail is the validator id bun_design_system_detector (bunOnly). Severity 2 / strict disposition stays in core:verification as rule data.
